title: ‘A Servant Class, Not a Working Class’: Stephen Miller’s Biographer on What Comes Next
gist: After Republicans lost both chambers in the midterms, Trump named Stephen Miller White House chief of staff; his biographer Jean Guerrero expects Miller to double down rather than moderate, widening the immigration crackdown into a campaign against immigrants' citizen allies in partnership with surveillance firms and tech billionaires. Guerrero now frames Miller less as a white nationalist than as a class supremacist and a case study in oligarchic capture.

insights.claim: Donald Trump named Stephen Miller, previously deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, as White House chief of staff days after midterm elections gave Democrats majorities in both the Senate and House.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Miller will likely shape the White House agenda for the remaining two years under divided government; expect executive-action-heavy policy rather than legislation.
insights.locator: Last week, President Donald Trump named

insights.claim: Biographer Jean Guerrero argues Miller has long wielded disproportionate power regardless of title and was the predictable pick for chief of staff as Trump's longest-lasting and most trusted adviser.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Signals continuity and concentration of policy control in one adviser; policy direction can be inferred from Miller's track record.
insights.quote: he has been the most effective sycophant in Trump's orbit
insights.locator: Stephen Miller has had a disproportionate amount

insights.claim: Guerrero believes Trump is turning to Miller's anti-immigrant scapegoating playbook to recover from the midterm defeat, but predicts it will not work this time because the public is horrified by how far the immigration crackdown has already gone.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Diminishing political returns on immigration messaging could raise the odds of policy backlash, litigation and further electoral losses for Republicans.
insights.quote: I suspect that this time it's not going to work
insights.locator: I think Trump is hoping that Stephen Miller

insights.claim: Guerrero expects the unpopularity of ICE violence, including the Minneapolis shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, to push Miller to double down rather than change course, with any restraint limited to the performative side of the cruelty.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Do not price in moderation of immigration enforcement under a Miller-led White House.
insights.quote: I see it as an impetus for him to double down, absolutely.
insights.locator: I see it as an impetus

insights.claim: Guerrero predicts Miller will shift focus toward a war on the allies of immigrants, seeking to characterize social-justice activists broadly as domestic terrorists.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Watch for terrorism-framed enforcement against NGOs and activists, with knock-on legal and civil-liberties risk for organizations that fund or host them.
insights.locator: If there's any restraint at all

insights.claim: Guerrero expects Miller to pursue the crackdown in collaboration with surveillance companies and aligned tech billionaires, continuing attacks on the right to privacy and free speech.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Surveillance-tech vendors with government contracts stand to gain demand, while facing reputational and regulatory risk as privacy and speech fights intensify.
insights.quote: I think Miller is going to do this in collaboration with surveillance companies and the tech billionaires
insights.locator: I think Miller is going to do this

insights.claim: Miller was heavily influenced by The Camp of the Saints, a white-supremacist French dystopian novel in which the villains include not only arriving immigrants but the citizens who ally with them.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The novel offers a lens for anticipating Miller's targeting of citizen allies, not just migrants.
insights.locator: Stephen Miller was very influenced by the book

insights.claim: Guerrero has revised her view of Miller from fundamentally a white nationalist to a class supremacist and a case study in oligarchic capture.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Policy may be better predicted by labor-hierarchy and oligarchic interests than by ethnonationalism alone.
insights.quote: now I see him more as a class supremacist and as a case study in oligarchic capture
insights.locator: My understanding of him has really changed.

insights.claim: Guerrero says the administration's interventions in Venezuela and in Honduras's elections, actions known to drive instability and migration, made sense to her only after Miller told Jake Tapper the world is governed by strength, force and power.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Expect a force-first Latin America foreign policy that may increase regional instability and migration pressure despite the stated border goals.
insights.quote: that is governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power
insights.locator: I came to this conclusion because

insights.claim: Guerrero argues the focus on criminalizing immigrants keeps one segment of the workforce in the shadows so it cannot join other workers in demanding dignity, implying the immigration agenda functions to suppress labor power.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: An enforcement regime that keeps undocumented workers precarious bears on wage pressure and labor organizing in immigrant-heavy sectors.
insights.quote: Stephen Miller wants a servant class, not a working class.
insights.locator: By focusing all the attention on the war on immigrants
